handled_verified.description: Node types the analyzer processes with probe/fixture-confirmed emission or correct routing (2026-08-31 ruby wave; pattern family added 2026-09-01 RUBYG1) alias keyword added 2026-09-07 RUBD15.

internal_silent.description: Container/literal/keyword types correctly emitting nothing (literals are payload, not relationships). Pattern-matching families now handled: bindings bind locals (RUBYG1 closed), guards/matches are walked for calls.

_notes.ERROR: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct. The analyzer DOES consult it — the error-collection walk reads `n.type === "ERROR" || n.isMissing` (src/ast/real-ruby-analyzer.ts:421-425) — but NO committed ruby fixture produces an ERROR node, so a `handled_verified` row would be a claim with no witness (`verify-fixture-coverage` reads `uncovered: ERROR` and blocks release). Recorded silent with this reason instead of trusted: authoring a ruby error-recovery fixture moves this row to handled_verified.
_notes.MISSING: produced by every tree-sitter parser and not a construct: tree-sitter marks an ABSENT required token with `isMissing` on the TOKEN'S OWN type, so the string "MISSING" is never a node type a fixture can contain — a `handled_verified` row would read `uncovered: MISSING` forever. The lane's error walk does read `isMissing` off the whole tree (real-ruby-analyzer.ts:421-425); every lane in the fleet records that read with this same row, so the class is named here rather than claimed. A node type that no fixture can witness is not evidence, and a bucket has to say which of the two it means.

gap.description: All confirmed gaps closed as of 2026-09-01

decisions.question: When is an instance_variable a READ (uses) vs a WRITE?
decisions.resolution: instance_variable as the FIRST child of an assignment/operator_assignment is a WRITE (never a use). All other positions are READS emitting uses (family contract: csharp/dart/swift/objc/php precedent). Verified: @total = x emits nothing; @total + x emits one use.

decisions.question: Is Ruby 3 pattern-matching binding extraction in scope for M14?
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION: pattern destructure bindings are parsed but not modeled as symbols/uses; calls inside match bodies are still captured. Tracked as RUBYG1 for a future wave.

decisions.question: Do @@class_vars and $globals emit uses like instance_variable?
decisions.resolution: NO — declared limitation: @@var/$var are file-global and cross-file by nature; per-file emission would fabricate cross-file semantics. Only instance_variable emits member-read uses.

decisions.question: Does @x += v emit a uses edge for @x, or is every operator_assignment LHS a pure write?
decisions.resolution: EMITS USES — read-modify-write reads @x before writing it. Plain assignment (@x = v) stays a pure write. Verified in rake corpus (@balance += amount, @options ||= {}): fixture pins authorize->@balance x3 and refund->@balance x1; oracle already mirrored this rule.

decisions.question: Do methods inside class << self belong to the enclosing class?
decisions.resolution: YES — grammar represents them as ordinary method nodes inside singleton_class; analyzer re-parents them to the enclosing class with isStatic/isSingleton metadata. Verified: def self.create emits Service.create static.

decisions.question: Do postfix (modifier) conditionals count toward cyclomatic complexity?
decisions.resolution: YES — postfix forms are genuine branches, semantically identical to the block forms (`return false if x` == `if x; return false; end`) and Ruby's most idiomatic branching. tree-sitter-ruby emits DISTINCT node types (if_modifier etc.) that the analyzer previously skipped, under-reporting every modifier-heavy method. Both the per-symbol counter and the file-level cyclomaticComplexity now count if/unless/while/until/rescue + their *_modifier forms. Verified: fixture authorize has 2 if_modifier + 1 while = complexity 4 (previously mis-pinned at 2); charge has 1 if_modifier = 2 (previously mis-pinned at 1).

decisions.node_type: case_match / in_clause / array_pattern / hash_pattern / as_pattern (pattern family)
decisions.question: What do Ruby 3 pattern-matching bindings emit?
decisions.resolution: BINDINGS ARE LOCALS, NEVER EDGES — same contract as left_assignment_list destructuring: `in [a, b]` binds a/b as locals of the match scope (visible in guards and match bodies); `in {name:}` binds name via hash_key_symbol (shorthand); `{age: x}` binds x; `Integer => n` binds n; `in x` binds x; `[*head, last]` binds head/last. `variable_reference_pattern` (^n) PINNS an outer local and binds nothing. Before RUBG1 the bindings leaked as bogus calls:a/calls:b edges in both the pattern and match body — now forbidden by fixture pins and the ruby/pattern-bindings-leak-as-calls mutant.

decisions.question: Do the __LINE__/__FILE__/__encoding__ keyword tokens produce distinct parse-tree nodes in the pinned grammar?
decisions.resolution: No. Probe-verified 2026-09-02: all three keyword tokens parse as plain `identifier` nodes in every context (assignment, call args, bare expression). The grammar declares the rules but the parser folds them into identifier. Analyzer needs no distinct handling; values remain available via text. Reclassified from handled_verified per the F6 fixture-coverage gate (M14.0.F6).

decisions.question: Is test_pattern a realizable parse-tree node for valid Ruby pattern-matching source in the pinned grammar?
decisions.resolution: No. Probe-verified 2026-09-02 across 20+ case/in shapes (call patterns, bare literals, ranges, one-line `then` forms, parenthesized alts): the only source that produced test_pattern was `def m(v) = case v in 1 then 2 end`, which is an ERROR parse — the one-line case/in form is not supported by this grammar version. Every clean parse realizes other pattern nodes (as_pattern, alternative_pattern, parenthesized_pattern, find_pattern). Reclassified from handled_verified per the F6 fixture-coverage gate (M14.0.F6).

decisions.question: AnalyzeContext.overrideCompanion is never populated by production callers — what must the analyzer do for externally-declared bases?
decisions.resolution: M37.10 ruling (family-wide): the companion is optional enrichment, never a hard gate. In-file base declaring the method -> verified override @0.95; companion present -> companion-index resolution; otherwise deterministic Pass-3 first-parent guess @0.5 with reasonCode 'first-parent-guess' and tier 'inferred' — below the patterns.ts 0.7 threshold, counted as heuristic by the F5 differential. Gating on the companion alone silently dropped every cross-file override. Gated by F9-PROBE-M3710-RUBY, the ruby/external-override fixture + confidence pins, and 6 family regression mutants.

decisions.node_type: call with expression receiver (.new on Class.new{...})
decisions.question: `Class.new { ... }.new` (and any .new whose receiver is a call/block expression) has no nameable class — what edge, if any, must be emitted?
decisions.resolution: None. Rack two-corpus wave 2026-09: the outer .new constructs an ANONYMOUS class; the analyzer leaked a junk `calls:<owner> -> new` at top level (3 fabrications in spec_lock.rb) while the oracle truth emits nothing (no enclosing class). Analyzer now suppresses expression-receiver .new that cannot resolve to a constant/owner; `self.new`/`self.class.new` inside a class still resolve to the enclosing class (instantiates), and lowercase receivers (`task_class.new`) remain genuine calls:new — all mirrored by deriveRubyEdges.

decisions.question: Do default-argument VALUE expressions (`def f(app, lock = Lock.new)`, `def g(env, app = @app)`) count as call/use/instantiation sites of the method?
decisions.resolution: Yes — Ruby evaluates defaults in the method scope at call time. Rack two-corpus wave 2026-09: only the body was walked, dropping mutex = Mutex.new (instantiates), params = Rack::Utils.default_query_parser (calls), app = @app (uses). walkParamDefaults now walks optional/keyword parameter values under the method owner; oracle truth already did. Locals in default values resolve as method calls unless they name a parameter (parity fix: collectLocals adds param NAMES only, not identifiers inside default values — handler.rb `www_authenticate = challenge`).

decisions.question: `class X < Struct.new(:root, :path, :files)` — the superclass is a call, not a constant. What edges exist?
decisions.resolution: No extends (the base is anonymous/unnameable — both sides agree the leaf- extends edge is noise), but the `Struct.new` call IS a declaration-time instantiation of Struct and must surface. Rack two-corpus wave 2026-09 (directory.rb DirectoryBody): analyzer now visits call nodes inside the superclass field under the declaration's outer scope, mirroring deriveRubyEdges which already walked the superclass subtree.

decisions.question: Member reads with no enclosing def (spec/DSL `it`/`before` blocks, bare class-level reads) — do they emit uses, and under which source?
decisions.resolution: Yes, under the file-level owner (owner || Global) — the same fallback calls use. Rack two-corpus wave 2026-09 (spec_media_type.rb @content_type/@empty_hash reads): walkBody only fired inside defs, so spec-DSL member reads vanished while the oracle truth counts every instance_variable read. The class/top-level DFS now emits memberRead uses for reads (assignment/operator-assignment LHS still skipped, SCD1 family contract).

decisions.question: `alias_method :local_path, :path` — the analyzer emits calls:<alias> with aliasedTo metadata; the oracle truth had no mirror, flagging it unexplained. Keep, mirror, or remove?
decisions.resolution: Keep and mirror. The alias makes the alias name a callable member of the class — the analyzer contract (calls source=class target=alias, aliasedTo metadata) has shipped since before M37.10 and carries the graph information. deriveRubyEdges now emits calls:<alias> for two-simple_symbol alias_method, matching the analyzer. Rack two-corpus wave 2026-09 (uploaded_file.rb local_path).

decisions.question: Are hash/argument pair VALUES real expression positions whose method calls must be emitted?
decisions.resolution: YES — `{ key: fetch_key }` (colon), `{ pair => fetch_val }` (rocket, key AND value both evaluate), and `store.write(cache: build_entry)` (keyword argument) values are expressions evaluated at runtime; a bare identifier there is a method call when not a local. The `pair` entry in BARE_CALL_SKIP_PARENTS (analyzer) and the oracle skip list silently suppressed EVERY value-position call on BOTH sides — a shared blind spot F5 cannot see (matching is label+target, so equal suppression never shows as missing/unexplained). Pair removed from both skip lists; colon-form KEYS are hash_key_symbol nodes (never identifiers) so only genuine value expressions changed. Locals stay silent. Master-review 2026-09, pinned by ruby/master-review-wave fixture + mutant ruby/readd-pair-value-suppression.

decisions.node_type: class/module reopen with namespaced name (class A::B, module A::B) + call-expression superclasses
decisions.question: What identity does a namespaced reopen declaration carry, and when is a superclass statically nameable?
decisions.resolution: (1) `class M::Inner` declares the SAME class as nested `module M; class Inner` — symbol name = LEAF, ownerName = the module-scope path (kept verbatim, e.g. A::B), fqn metadata records the full declaration text. Before this the reopen carried the full path as a bare name with no owner, so the two spellings never unified across files (rake's lib uses both styles). (2) A superclass is statically nameable only as a constant/scope path (`Foo`, `::Foo`, `A::B`) — call expressions (`Struct.new(...)`, `Class.new(Base)`) have an ANONYMOUS base: no extends (RB-C ruling was violated by the analyzer emitting the raw expression text; the oracle produced a DIFFERENT junk target — latent missing+unexplained). Single source of truth: exported isRubyStaticSuperclassName (pure char scan, shared by analyzer and deriveRubyEdges — a duplicated inline regex drifted). Master-review 2026-09, pinned by ruby/master-review-wave (Tuple/Child/Inner symbols) + mutant ruby/readd-dynamic-superclass-extends.

decisions.node_type: override resolution with leaf-colliding external superclass (class Rake::TestCase < Test::Unit::TestCase)
decisions.question: How must the override pass treat a superclass whose leaf name equals the declaring class's own leaf?
decisions.resolution: A class can never extend itself, so when the leaf-collapsed base equals the class's own identity the base is NOT a verified in-file base — routing it through the verified branch fabricated self-overrides at 0.95 (rake helper.rb: 9 phantom edges). Such a base is external-with-same-leaf: emit only the honest 0.5 first-parent guess (heuristic, excluded from unexplained), same as any other undeclared base. NOTE: an in-file base with the same leaf as a namespaced subclass in the SAME file is an inherent ambiguity of the name-keyed override map and is documented, not resolved. Master-review 2026-09, pinned by ruby/master-review-wave forbid overrides@0.95 + mutant ruby/self-verify-overrides-guard.

decisions.question: What does the keyword `alias` emit at declaration scope, and what inside method bodies?
decisions.resolution: Declaration scope (class/module/top-level): the RB-E alias_method contract — calls:<newname> with aliasedTo:<oldname> (+ keywordAlias:true marker); before this the keyword form was invisible while alias_method was handled. Method-body aliases are runtime redefinitions and emit NOTHING on either side — `alias` added to both skip lists so the two identifiers no longer fabricate junk bare calls (analyzer emitted them pre-wave; the oracle mirrored the junk). `setter` (the name wrapper of `def size=`) likewise added to the analyzer skip list to stop nested setter names leaking as bare calls. Master-review 2026-09, pinned by ruby/master-review-wave calls:Api->copy + mutant ruby/drop-keyword-alias-edge.

decisions.question: Ruby second review (2026-09-13): endless `def f = expr` has no body_statement, so whole bodies were never walked (`def fetch = client.get` emitted nothing while the oracle derived calls->get).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: walkMethodBody falls back to non-name/params children with params bound; def-name skip made positional (first named child) on both sides so endless bare-identifier bodies read. Fixture expects calls fetch->get and label->name; mutant endless-body-silence CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Ruby second review (2026-09-13): `defined?(bar)` parses as a unary node (not a call), so the operand leaked as calls->bar; `undef helper` leaked calls->helper. Both are unevaluated/name positions, never calls or reads.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: skip defined?-unary subtrees (pre-scan and DFS) and undef subtrees. Fixture forbids calls check->other, uses check->@cfg, calls check->helper; mutants defined-probe-reads and undef-name-calls CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Ruby second review (2026-09-13): only simple_symbol attr args registered properties; bare strings (`attr_reader "name"`, legal Ruby) were dropped.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: accept string args (quote-stripped). Fixture expects property name; mutant attr-string-loss CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Ruby second review (2026-09-13): `Point = Struct.new(:x)` (likewise Data.define/Class.new/Module.new) left no symbol — the defined type was invisible and Point.new resolved against nothing.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: LHS constant of a factory call emits Class (Struct/Data/Class) or Module (Module.new) instead of Constant, at class level and top level. Block-defined methods keep the enclosing owner (documented residual). Fixture expects classes Point and Cfg; mutant struct-new-symbols-loss CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Ruby second review (2026-09-13): `autoload :JsonParser, "json/parser"` recorded nothing (the call itself is builtin-skipped, correctly).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: record the require-shaped import + references edge for string paths (dynamic paths skipped like require). Fixture expects both; mutant autoload-import-loss CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Ruby second review, lane triage (2026-09-13): `def result.name` / `def @rio.check?` — receiver-precedes-name broke the positional def-name skip (oracle emitted calls->name), and neither side visited receivers (`@rio` reads at definition time).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED both sides: name-field match with positional fallback for def names; singleton receivers visited (ivar receivers emit member reads, identifier/constant/self receivers stay silent as before). Oracle scopes nested-def name+receiver to the enclosing method id. Fixture expects hook->@cfg and forbids hook->cached/memo/obj; lanes re-verified 0/0.

decisions.question: Are Ruby's include/prepend/extend conformance (implements) or superclass inheritance (extends), as the family previously adapted them?
decisions.resolution: NEITHER: they are MODULE MIXIN COMPOSITION. include/prepend compose the module into the class's ancestor chain and extend composes it into the singleton class; the canonical vocabulary has exactly one value for that construct, mixes_in (Dart's `with` is the measured population of the same value). include/prepend -> mixes_in (role include/prepend), extend -> mixes_in (role extend); implements is NOT APPLICABLE for Ruby (no interface/conformance production, no enforcement) and `class B < A` / factory Class.new(Base) stay `extends`. Relabel at UNCHANGED construct sites with the delta measured: cap-50 implements 17 -> 0, extends 48 -> 44, mixes_in 0 -> 21 = 17 + 4 EXACTLY, TABLE 1 totals byte-identical; evidence tier on the relabelled rows is structural (classifyEvidenceTier follows the construct).
decisions.decided_by: owner-delegated (ALL-OUT-OF-ALL phase 2, task-13, lane ruling with the C/Dart relabel precedent)

label_coverage._description: Which relationship labels this lane actually COMPARES, and which admitted labels have no oracle behind them. Measured by script/m14/verify-label-coverage.ts and script/m14/verify-truth-existence.ts.

declared_no_truth.label: overrides
declared_no_truth.reason: `overrides` sits in the differential allowlist DEFAULT admitted prefix for every language except csharp/dart/swift/cpp, so it is compared for this lane — but this lane has no overrides oracle, so every analyzer overrides row enters the comparison with no truth to meet and is counted as an unexplained FABRICATION. That number accuses the analyzer of inventing edges when the real gap is that nobody wrote down what it should have produced. Dropping the label instead would hide the analyzer's output, which is the other half of the same silence. Closes when an overrides oracle exists for this language (scala's own cross-file work is recorded as SDJ-8); until then the state is DECLARED rather than counted as a verdict.
declared_no_truth.closes_when: an overrides oracle exists for this language; then admit it and reconcile

excluded.label: implements
excluded.from: The pinned tree-sitter-ruby grammar (wasm/tree-sitter-ruby.wasm, sha256 93a5022855314cdb...) has no interface/conformance production: 0 of its 108 distinct named types is an interface or conformance construct (no interface/implement/implements_clause/super_interfaces nodes; the 176 anonymous tokens carry no such keyword either). Ruby duck typing is not a declared conformance, so no declaration can satisfy an interface.
